# Sequential counter encoding for "at least k of n variables are true"
def at_least_k(solver, vars_list, k, next_var):
    """Encode at least k of vars_list are true using sequential counter"""
    n_vars = len(vars_list)
    # s[i][j] means at least j of the first i variables are true
    # s[i][j] is a new variable
    
    s = {}
    for i in range(n_vars + 1):
        for j in range(k + 1):
            s[(i, j)] = next_var
            next_var += 1
    
    # Base cases
    # s[0][0] = true
    solver.add_clause([s[(0, 0)]])
    for j in range(1, k + 1):
        solver.add_clause([-s[(0, j)]])  # s[0][j] = false for j > 0
    
    # Recursive cases
    for i in range(1, n_vars + 1):
        for j in range(k + 1):
            # s[i][j] = s[i-1][j] OR (s[i-1][j-1] AND vars[i-1])
            # This gives us:
            # s[i][j] >= s[i-1][j]
            # s[i][j] >= s[i-1][j-1] AND vars[i-1]
            # s[i][j] <= s[i-1][j] OR (s[i-1][j-1] AND vars[i-1])
            
            # s[i][j] >= s[i-1][j]
            solver.add_clause([-s[(i-1, j)], s[(i, j)]])
            
            if j > 0:
                # s[i][j] >= s[i-1][j-1] AND vars[i-1]
                solver.add_clause([-s[(i-1, j-1)], -vars_list[i-1], s[(i, j)]])
                
                # s[i][j] <= s[i-1][j] OR (s[i-1][j-1] AND vars[i-1])
                # Equivalent to: NOT s[i][j] OR s[i-1][j] OR (s[i-1][j-1] AND vars[i-1])
                # Which is: (NOT s[i][j] OR s[i-1][j] OR s[i-1][j-1]) AND (NOT s[i][j] OR s[i-1][j] OR vars[i-1])
                solver.add_clause([-s[(i, j)], s[(i-1, j)], s[(i-1, j-1)]])
                solver.add_clause([-s[(i, j)], s[(i-1, j)], vars_list[i-1]])
    
    # Result: s[n_vars][k] must be true
    return s[(n_vars, k)], next_var
